forecaster_note: Winds will go mostly offshore until about 9/10am. Northern Beaches seeing WSW winds and clean surf for pretty much every spot. Big range of sizes across the breaks: well OH – 2x OH at S magnets, head high or so to a little OH for north ends, waist high in sheltered corners. Later AM winds go onshore. – Surfline forecast team. Water temp is estimated (no live station feed this run).

wind.summary: 20km/h SW offshore at Dee Why and Manly till ~10am, then swings onshore. Cross-shore at Long Reef and Curl Curl from the start.

shark.summary: No shark detections anywhere on the Northern Beaches (Palm Beach to Manly) in the last 24 hours. Feed is live — newest NSW detection 3.2h old, 22 statewide in 24h.

days.label: Today
days.note: Serious day. 10.8ft @ 10s from dead south (174°) carrying 1,605 kJ average and peaking 2,875 — 100% consistency, so it's relentless. The difference from Wednesday is the wind: SW offshore till about 10am. Dee Why is the pick because the S angle undercuts it down to a rideable 4–10ft while Long Reef maxes out. Window closes hard at 10am.

dee-why.window: Now till 10am. Low tide was 5:16am so it's filling — mid-tide push is the sweet spot before the 12:03pm high fattens it.
alerts: ⚠️ Big and powerful — 1,605 kJ average, 2,875 kJ peak
Dead-south 174° means heavy shifting sets; size range is wide

tip.label: Frontside, and pick your set
tip.text: Rare combination: real energy AND offshore wind at your home break. The Point rights are frontside — sit deeper than feels comfortable and commit early, because at 10s the sets stand up fast and won't let you correct. Don't get greedy with the 10ft outliers; the 4–6ft ones have the best shape.

long-reef.window: No window. Fully S-exposed and cross-shore from dawn — maxed beyond usable shape.
alerts: ⚠️ 8–15ft and cross-shore — heavy rips, not a surf

curl-curl.window: Marginal. Cross-shore SW from first light and the size is inconsistent between banks. Dee Why is the better call.
alerts: ⚠️ Wide size range, cross-shore wind — hard to read

manly.window: Now till 10am — the mellower offshore option if 4–10ft at Dee Why is more than you want today.

tip.label: Backside fallback
tip.text: Headland knocks the S swell down to something you can actually work with, and the wind is offshore here too. North Steyne lefts are backside — the smaller, cleaner version of today.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: The best all-round day of the week. Size settles to a workable 3–7ft, energy drops to 181 kJ but consistency stays at 100% — so it's steady, not lucky. Light 6–8km/h W offshore till about 11am, then a NE sea breeze textures it. If you can only get out once before the weekend, make it this morning.

dee-why.window: Dawn–11am, the longest clean window of the week. Light W offshore at 6km/h — glassy.

tip.label: The one to plan around
tip.text: Clean, consistent, and exactly the size where your frontside Point rights work best. Nothing to survive here — this is a day to actually surf well rather than just get through.

long-reef.window: Dawn–11am. Biggest of the four with the same light offshore — the standout if you want size with shape.

tip.label: Pick of the day
tip.text: Rated fair-good and holding a foot or two more than Dee Why. Worth the drive.

curl-curl.window: Dawn–11am. Open beach with light offshore — banks will be working after this week's swell reshaped them.

tip.label: Fresh banks
tip.text: Four days of heavy S swell will have rearranged the sandbanks. Worth a look on the way past — could be the best it's been in weeks.

manly.window: Dawn–11am. Smallest and most forgiving of the four.

tip.label: Mellow option
tip.text: Backside lefts at North Steyne, waist-to-chest and clean. Fine if you're tired after today.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Sunday has been upgraded hard since Tuesday's read — it was forecast at 45 kJ and knee-high, now it's 289 kJ with 19s long-period S swell and Long Reef at 4–8ft. Sunday is the weekend. Saturday is the lesser day: 125 kJ, consistency down to 63% mid-morning, long waits between sets, though it's clean all morning with W offshore. Both days offshore early; Sunday holds N/NW and stays clean most of the day with hot temps.

dee-why.window: Sun 6–10am is the call — 3–6ft with 19s groundswell behind it. Sat 6–11am is smaller (2–4ft) and patchy.
alerts: Saturday consistency drops to 63% mid-morning — long lulls
Sunday wind swings cross/onshore after 9am, so go early

long-reef.window: Sun 6–11am — 4–8ft, the standout of the weekend and holds the offshore longest. Sat 2–6ft with big gaps between sets.
alerts: Sunday is the pick of the two days by a clear margin

curl-curl.window: Sun 6–12pm — offshore right through to midday here, the longest window of the weekend. Sat 2–5ft.

manly.window: Sheltered from the S angle both days, so it stays small. Only worth it if you want something easy.
alerts: Smallest of the four all weekend — 1–3ft
